nodes.label: CI check matrix (Node 18/20/22/24, no npm install)

nodes.label: CI fall-through test per harness
nodes.rationale: A handler with no key must fall through — exit 0, empty stdout — once per harness environment: Claude Code (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT) and Codex CLI (PLUGIN_ROOT).

nodes.label: Pages build and deploy
nodes.rationale: Runs on push to main touching README, package.json, site/, hooks/, assets/ or the workflow; builds site/dist with npm run build:site after npm test, then deploys with actions/deploy-pages.

nodes.label: Release drift check
nodes.rationale: A merged release PR publishes nothing: the tag is the trigger and pushing it is manual. qrspi 0.1.1 sat on main untagged for a week and nothing said so. Fails when package.json version has no hookgate--v<version> tag once the commit that set it is older than a 2 h grace; runs on push and daily so a failing scheduled run emails the owner.

nodes.label: Constraints: state <= 32k tokens, 2 s latency budget
nodes.rationale: Truncate commands and messages; redact secret-looking values; explicit timeout, Jev promises 70-500 ms.
nodes.norm_label: constraints: state <= 32k tokens, 2 s latency budget

nodes.label: Done-when criteria
nodes.rationale: Plugin installable in any repo; PreToolUse on Bash returns allow|ask|deny with a reason; Stop returns block; fail-open on missing key; reproducible benchmark in evals/ with >=50 labelled commands; npm test validates manifests; CI on Node 18/20/22/24; release by tag as in qrspi.

nodes.label: Open risks (Codex ask, Jev calibration, jev-latest drift)
nodes.rationale: Codex has no ask on PreToolUse; Jev calibration on shell-command risk is unmeasured — under ~90% agreement the command gate stays ask-only; jev-latest can change answers, so the benchmark re-runs at every version.
nodes.norm_label: open risks (codex ask, jev calibration, jev-latest drift)

nodes.label: HG-1 brief — Jev in Claude Code gates
nodes.rationale: Brief from an interview on 2026-09-22; the input to the Questions phase. Goal: the small, frequent harness decisions taken by Jev in ~100 ms with calibrated confidence instead of an LLM or nobody.
nodes.norm_label: hg-1 brief — jev in claude code gates

nodes.label: Social preview OG card (1280x640)

nodes.label: Decision: gates in the harness, not a library for apps
nodes.rationale: Because that is the gap: TypeSafe covers apps.
nodes.norm_label: decision: gates in the harness, not a library for apps

nodes.label: Decision: name hookgate
nodes.rationale: Free on npm and GitHub on 2026-09-22, describes the thing; uses neither Jev nor TypeSafe, their marks.

nodes.label: Decision: new public repo, npm, the qrspi operating model
nodes.rationale: Because qrspi stays Markdown-only and does not tie its thesis to a vendor.

nodes.label: Two harnesses, one file (design accounts for Codex from the start)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code in 0.1.0, Codex CLI in 0.2.0; the handler reads the same stdin JSON on both and emits each harness answer shape chosen from the environment (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT vs PLUGIN_ROOT); two manifests, two hooks.json, no forked logic.
nodes.norm_label: two harnesses, one file (design accounts for codex from the start)

nodes.label: Decision: zero dependencies, native fetch
nodes.rationale: A hook starts on every tool call and must cost nothing at start-up; Node 18 has fetch.

nodes.label: Out of scope for HG-1
nodes.rationale: Teaching Jev, an SDK, PostToolUse hygiene, gating other tools, the Codex adapter itself, other harnesses, offline fallback, telemetry, auto-tuning, rewriting user permissions, second labeller, the site, Windows testing.

nodes.label: Q10 · How much Codex must exist in 0.1.0
nodes.rationale: Default: environment detection and one output-shaping function with a unit test per harness; no .codex-plugin manifest until Research confirms Codex event names and decision vocabulary.
nodes.norm_label: q10 · how much codex must exist in 0.1.0

nodes.label: Q1 · Does 0.1.0 emit allow at all
nodes.rationale: A false allow on a destructive command is the single worst outcome. Default: code emits all three; shipped default makes allow effectively unreachable until the benchmark justifies lowering it; deny is emitted from 0.1.0.
nodes.norm_label: q1 · does 0.1.0 emit allow at all

nodes.label: Q2 · May a repo config loosen the gate
nodes.rationale: A hostile repo config could turn the safety gate into an auto-approver. Default: user-level config sets the floor and owns fail-closed; a repo file may only tighten.
nodes.norm_label: q2 · may a repo config loosen the gate

nodes.label: Q3 · Who labels the benchmark commands and by what rule
nodes.rationale: The agreement percentage is only as good as the labels. Default: maintainer labels alone with a written rule in CONTRIBUTING (dangerous = irreversible loss or exfiltration outside repo; ask = reversible-but-consequential; safe = read-only or repo-local).
nodes.norm_label: q3 · who labels the benchmark commands and by what rule

nodes.label: Q4 · Is shipping every Bash command to a third-party API acceptable and what is redacted
nodes.rationale: Default: acceptable for the maintainer; README states what is sent; credential-looking values replaced with <redacted>; cwd sent as basename.
nodes.norm_label: q4 · is shipping every bash command to a third-party api acceptable and what is redacted

nodes.label: Q5 · How many times may the Stop gate block per turn
nodes.rationale: A looping block burns the tokens the plugin exists to save. Default: at most one block per stop sequence; on stop_hook_active exit 0 without calling Jev.
nodes.norm_label: q5 · how many times may the stop gate block per turn

nodes.label: Q6 · What does git state mean for the Stop gate
nodes.rationale: Default: git status --porcelain capped at 50 lines, empty outside a repo; the transcript is not read in 0.1.0.
nodes.norm_label: q6 · what does git state mean for the stop gate

nodes.label: Q7 · Does the Stop gate call Jev on every stop
nodes.rationale: Default: a local prefilter for completion language first; only messages that pass go to Jev.
nodes.norm_label: q7 · does the stop gate call jev on every stop

nodes.label: Q9 · What does fail-closed return per gate
nodes.rationale: Default: fail-closed affects PreToolUse only and means ask, never deny; Stop always fail-open; timeout, non-2xx and malformed body all count as API down.
nodes.norm_label: q9 · what does fail-closed return per gate

nodes.label: Backlog issue sync (one-way)
nodes.rationale: BACKLOG.md is the single source of truth; issues are a view of it. Sync runs one way only, backlog to issues, never the reverse: editing or closing an issue on GitHub changes nothing, ticking the item in BACKLOG.md does. Runs only when BACKLOG.md, the script or the workflow change, plus on demand with dry_run. A concurrency group prevents two racing runs opening HG-n twice; the plan is printed before apply so the log says what it was about to do.

nodes.rationale: Design work for the first release, one fresh session per phase; rule 4: the brief does not enter Research.

nodes.label: HG-10 — Audit mode: log every decision without enforcing
nodes.rationale: In 0.1.0 because it is how the thresholds stop being guesses.
nodes.norm_label: hg-10 — audit mode: log every decision without enforcing

nodes.label: HG-11 — Codex CLI adapter: same handlers, Codex answer shape
nodes.rationale: Contract verified against learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks; ask passes through with a systemMessage; verified live 2026-09-22 on Codex 0.155.1; Codex dropped plugin-bundled hooks, so print-hooks writes the repo-level file.
nodes.norm_label: hg-11 — codex cli adapter: same handlers, codex answer shape

nodes.label: HG-12 — Per-session decision cache
nodes.rationale: Keyed by session_id and the redacted state hash, TTL, invalidated on cwd change; a repeat returns in under 5 ms and never outlives the session.

nodes.label: HG-14 — hookgate doctor
nodes.rationale: Answers "why is nothing happening"; non-zero only on a broken configuration, never on a slow API.

nodes.label: HG-15 — Screen tool results for injected instructions
nodes.rationale: One Noul on WebFetch, Read and Bash results; off by default until a fixture set gives the false-positive rate.
nodes.norm_label: hg-15 — screen tool results for injected instructions

nodes.label: HG-16 — Benchmark the optimisations: cache, promotion, thresholds
nodes.rationale: Half done 2026-09-22 without a key: overhead 59 ms p50, prefilter and cache ceilings, redactor 6%; still needed with a key: cost and latency with and without cache, the threshold sweep.
nodes.norm_label: hg-16 — benchmark the optimisations: cache, promotion, thresholds

nodes.label: HG-2 — Command-risk gate: PreToolUse on Bash answered by Jev
nodes.rationale: One Choice and one Noul on a redacted, truncated state; below threshold ask, never allow; a unit test per fail-open path runnable without a key.
nodes.norm_label: hg-2 — command-risk gate: pretooluse on bash answered by jev

nodes.label: HG-3 — Completion gate: Stop hook that blocks unverified claims of done
nodes.rationale: One Noul on last_assistant_message plus a capped git status; at most one block per stop so the agent cannot loop.
nodes.norm_label: hg-3 — completion gate: stop hook that blocks unverified claims of done

nodes.label: HG-6 — Site generated from README, as qrspi does it
nodes.rationale: site/build.mjs ported with the gates index read off hooks/hooks.json.
nodes.norm_label: hg-6 — site generated from readme, as qrspi does it

nodes.label: HG-8 — PostToolUse output hygiene (dropped)
nodes.rationale: A PostToolUse hook can only add additionalContext or block, never shorten a result already in context; a Noul saying "not worth keeping" adds tokens — net negative by construction. Output size is the harness's lever.

nodes.label: HG-9 — Fail-closed as an explicit opt-in
nodes.rationale: failClosed: true makes an unreachable API mean ask rather than fall-through; never the default.
nodes.norm_label: hg-9 — fail-closed as an explicit opt-in

nodes.label: v0.2.0 — Observe, promote, port
nodes.rationale: What the first run of the gates teaches, turned into features, plus the second harness.

nodes.label: Audit mode
nodes.rationale: Every gate judges for real, logs one JSON line per decision, and always falls through. The default until 0.1.0 because it is how thresholds stop being guesses.

nodes.label: Two harnesses, one file (Codex CLI adapter)
nodes.rationale: Same stdin JSON under Claude Code and Codex; Codex has no ask on PreToolUse so a below-threshold answer passes through with a systemMessage (codex.askAs: deny refuses instead); injection feedback via decision: block.
nodes.norm_label: two harnesses, one file (codex cli adapter)

nodes.label: Command-risk gate (PreToolUse on Bash)
nodes.rationale: Choice{allow, ask, deny} plus a Noul on destruction outside the repo; ask or deny with a reason.

nodes.label: Completion gate (Stop)
nodes.rationale: Noul on whether the last message claims a completion the visible state does not support, on the message plus git status; block with a reason naming what to verify, once per prompt.

nodes.label: Every config value is checked
nodes.rationale: A bad value is reported by doctor and the default takes its place, so the gate never runs arithmetic on a string.

nodes.label: Configuration trust order
nodes.rationale: Defaults, then ~/.hookgate.json, then HOOKGATE_CONFIG, then the repository file, then HOOKGATE_MODE / HOOKGATE_MODEL / HOOKGATE_FAIL_CLOSED.

nodes.label: failClosed opt-in
nodes.rationale: The explicit opt-in under which an unreachable API makes the command gate ask; never the default.

nodes.label: hookgate
nodes.rationale: Calibrated, sub-second decisions inside the agent harness: nobody had put a System One model inside the hooks; TypeSafe teaches Jev well already, so hookgate has one job the harness can feel rather than duplicating SDKs and cookbooks.

nodes.label: hookgate doctor
nodes.rationale: Key, connectivity, latency, model, config, harness; non-zero only on a broken configuration, never on a slow API.

nodes.label: hookgate report
nodes.rationale: Decisions by outcome, p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate, input tokens and cost per judged decision at TypeSafe's published price, ask share per threshold.

nodes.label: Injection screen (PostToolUse)
nodes.rationale: Noul on whether a tool output contains instructions addressed to an AI agent; additionalContext telling the agent to treat the span as data. Off by default until the fixture set gives a false-positive rate.

nodes.label: TypeSafe Jev (System One model)
nodes.rationale: Returns typed decisions with a calibrated confidence instead of text — no parsing, no hallucination to catch — in about 100 ms.

nodes.label: Per-session decision cache
nodes.rationale: The same command in the same session is judged once; measured ceiling ~0% (99 exact repeats in 27,111 commands) — it stays because it is free, not because it pays.

nodes.label: hookgate print-hooks
nodes.rationale: Codex 0.155 dropped plugin-bundled hooks, so the repo-level .codex/hooks.json is written with absolute paths.

nodes.label: qrspi (sibling project)
nodes.rationale: The model for hookgate: Markdown-first plugin, dependency-free installer, site generated from the README, releases by tag.

nodes.label: Codex CLI hooks contract (verified 2026-09-22)
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse has allow|deny only — no ask; PostToolUse has no additionalContext; Codex 0.155.1 removed plugin_hooks, so hooks are repo- or user-level with absolute paths and need persisted trust.

nodes.label: Jev API facts (read 2026-09-22)
nodes.rationale: POST /v1/systemone; noul, choice, score; confidence 0-1; model jev-1.13.0; 64k tokens per request, 32k for state; $42 per billion input tokens; dated because they are someone else's product.

nodes.label: Local loop (npm test == check)
nodes.rationale: The check validates the manifests and versions, hooks.json events/commands/timeouts, the fail-open statement in the README and the files the tarball ships; CI runs it on Node 18/20/22/24 without npm install.

nodes.label: Codex, live (2026-09-22, 0.155.1)
nodes.rationale: git push --force → ask at 0.85, passed through; rm -rf ~/… → deny at 0.97, blocked; Stop gate ran. Two surprises: plugin_hooks removed, repo hooks need trust — print-hooks and the Install section come from that.

nodes.label: HG-1 design notes, as implemented
nodes.rationale: Not QRSPI artifacts: the gates were implemented directly on 2026-09-22 from the brief; these are the decisions taken on the way so the brief and the code agree.

nodes.label: Every hook has a timeout of at most 10 s
nodes.rationale: Set explicitly in hooks.json because the harness default is 600 s; the handler's own fetch timeout is shorter; check enforces the first.
nodes.norm_label: every hook has a timeout of at most 10 s

nodes.label: Names are not TypeSafe's marks
nodes.rationale: The project is hookgate; "Jev" and "TypeSafe" appear only when naming their product.

nodes.label: Below threshold is ask, never allow
nodes.rationale: Confidence decides whether to act, the answer decides what; low confidence always lands on the human.
nodes.norm_label: below threshold is ask, never allow

nodes.label: Fail-open
nodes.rationale: No key, no network, timeout, 5xx or a bug means no decision — exit 0, empty stdout — and the harness's normal permission flow applies. A gate that stalls the agent is worse than none.

nodes.label: hookgate narrows, never widens
nodes.rationale: A confident allow passes through by default; only allowMode: "allow" lets the plugin auto-approve, and audit mode never decides at all.

nodes.label: Repository config may only tighten
nodes.rationale: A repository you just cloned cannot switch the gate off, go audit, lower a threshold or point at a model or timeout that would fail open; it may enable a gate, raise a bar, go enforce, turn failClosed on, add lexicon patterns, ask Codex to deny.

nodes.label: Zero runtime dependencies
nodes.rationale: A hook starts on every tool call; start-up cost is the cost, so there is nothing to install, nothing to resolve, one file to read.

nodes.label: Audit mode is a mode, not a flag per gate
nodes.rationale: Same requests, same thresholds, always fall through, everything logged; the log is the second data source for the benchmark and the only honest way to pick thresholds.
nodes.norm_label: audit mode is a mode, not a flag per gate

nodes.label: Codex is an answer shape, not a fork
nodes.rationale: Detection by PLUGIN_ROOT, HOOKGATE_HARNESS or the stdin shape; the first cut turned ask into block, which narrowed more than the judgement supports, so ask now passes through with a systemMessage.
nodes.norm_label: codex is an answer shape, not a fork

nodes.label: Stop guard is double
nodes.rationale: stop_hook_active from the harness plus a per-prompt marker in the session file, so a block can never loop the agent.

nodes.label: HG-8 dropped by construction
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot make a tool result smaller after the fact; a Noul about "worth keeping" would spend tokens to say tokens were wasted; the PostToolUse slot goes to the one question that earns it, injected instructions.

nodes.label: Passthrough on allow
nodes.rationale: A PreToolUse allow bypasses the harness's own prompt, so by default a confident allow emits no decision — hookgate only narrows; allowMode: "allow" opts in once the benchmark says the gate earns it.

nodes.label: Cache keyed by gate + cwd + redacted state
nodes.rationale: TTL one hour, capped at 500 entries, never shared across sessions: a decision about rm -rf build/ in one repo says nothing about another.
nodes.norm_label: cache keyed by gate + cwd + redacted state

nodes.label: Two questions per command, not one
nodes.rationale: The Choice carries the verdict; a separate Noul on destruction outside the repo is the safety net that turns a confident allow into ask when the two disagree. One call answers both.
nodes.norm_label: two questions per command, not one

nodes.label: Errors are typed (JevError.code)
nodes.rationale: no-key · timeout · http · malformed · network; every one ends in fall-through; failClosed turns all but no-key into ask on the command gate only.

nodes.label: Tag convention hookgate--v*
nodes.rationale: Tags of the form hookgate--vX.Y.Z trigger the release; workflow_dispatch takes an existing tag for reruns.

nodes.label: HG-17 — Say exactly what leaves the machine
nodes.rationale: A plugin that POSTs shell commands and final messages to a third party owes the reader the list, per gate and field by field; check requires the README section.
nodes.norm_label: hg-17 — say exactly what leaves the machine

nodes.label: HG-18 — Bounded, atomic on-disk state
nodes.rationale: The audit log grew without limit and racing hooks could tear a session file; log rotates at 8 MB, sessions written to a temp file and renamed, pruned after seven days.

nodes.label: HG-19 — End-to-end tests of the CLI contract
nodes.rationale: HOOKGATE_ENDPOINT lets e2e tests spawn the real binary against a local fake Jev and assert JSON, header, that the session id never leaves, that a dead endpoint and garbage stdin fail open.
nodes.norm_label: hg-19 — end-to-end tests of the cli contract

nodes.label: HG-20 — CHANGELOG.md
nodes.rationale: Keep a Changelog with HG-n ids; check requires an [Unreleased] section and one for the current version.

nodes.label: HG-21 — Supply chain: CodeQL and pinned actions
nodes.rationale: CodeQL security-extended on push, PR and weekly; Renovate pins every uses: to a digest.
nodes.norm_label: hg-21 — supply chain: codeql and pinned actions

nodes.label: HG-22 — Knowledge graph of the repository (graphify)
nodes.rationale: Versioned so an agent can graphify query instead of re-reading files; 50 dangling-endpoint edges known.
nodes.norm_label: hg-22 — knowledge graph of the repository (graphify)

nodes.label: HG-31 — Release 0.0.3: everything on main, audit mode by default
nodes.rationale: First release through npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no token). mode defaults to audit so the release honours the v0.1.0 rule — nothing blocks on unmeasured thresholds; enforce is one line in ~/.hookgate.json.
nodes.norm_label: hg-31 — release 0.0.3: everything on main, audit mode by default

nodes.label: HG-4 — Benchmark: labelled commands, Jev gate vs type: prompt hook
nodes.rationale: Fundamental: gates the release and every default beyond ask; under ~90% agreement the command gate ships ask-only. Blocked on a TypeSafe API key since 2026-09-22.
nodes.norm_label: hg-4 — benchmark: labelled commands, jev gate vs type: prompt hook

nodes.label: HG-5 — First release 0.1.0: trusted publisher, tag, publish
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap done (0.0.2 by hand, 0.0.3 over the trusted publisher); what remains is HG-4, the default back to enforce, and the tag — after HG-4, not before.
nodes.norm_label: hg-5 — first release 0.1.0: trusted publisher, tag, publish

nodes.label: HG-7 — Backlog as the single source of truth, enforced by CI
nodes.rationale: scripts/backlog.mjs (lint, roadmap, check, issues), generated ROADMAP.md, one-way issue sync.
nodes.norm_label: hg-7 — backlog as the single source of truth, enforced by ci

nodes.label: Stable HG-n ids
nodes.rationale: The id never changes; a new item takes the next free number, never a retired one; moving between milestones is fine, renumbering is not. ver=dropped keeps the reasoning on record.

nodes.label: v0.1.0 — Two gates, one benchmark
nodes.rationale: The benchmark is the gate on this milestone: nothing ships as enforce by default, no threshold moves, no tag before HG-4 has run; blocked on a TypeSafe API key as of 2026-09-22.

nodes.label: v0.1.1 — Audit of 2026-09-22
nodes.rationale: A read of the whole tree with a security, privacy and robustness eye; all shipped the same day, kept as items so the ids stay in the CHANGELOG.

nodes.label: One-way issue sync (backlog-issues.yml)
nodes.rationale: On every push to main that changes BACKLOG.md issues are opened, retitled, closed and reopened to match; closing an issue on GitHub changes nothing.

nodes.label: Release 0.0.2 — 2026-09-22
nodes.rationale: The scaffold: manifests, inert handlers, check, CI, release by tag over trusted publishing, Pages site, BACKLOG.md. 0.0.1 is burnt on npm by a version published and unpublished in March.

nodes.label: Repository knowledge graph (graphify-out/)
nodes.rationale: Versioned so a session can ask before it reads; 367 nodes, 757 edges, 14 communities; 50 dangling edges where docs name code symbols differently from the AST.

nodes.label: scripts/backlog.mjs (lint · roadmap · check · issues)
nodes.rationale: The planner is tested against fixtures without a network call, because its failure modes are all decisions: a duplicate opened on every push, an issue closed for work still open.

nodes.label: --baseline: type: prompt judge on claude-opus-5
nodes.rationale: One claude -p per command, timed and costed from the CLI's own usage report; needs a logged-in claude.

nodes.label: release-drift.yml
nodes.rationale: Fails when main carries a version with no tag for two hours.

nodes.label: Benchmark
nodes.rationale: The Jev half is not run yet — it needs a TypeSafe API key; what has been measured is the incumbent, the plugin's own overhead (~60 ms) and counts from 102 real sessions.

nodes.label: Confidence thresholds
nodes.rationale: Scale with risk as TypeSafe's confidence guide recommends; defaults conservative, the benchmark moves them.

nodes.label: type: prompt hook (incumbent)
nodes.rationale: A full LLM call per decision — seconds and cents each; measured at 3,532 ms p50 and $0.129 per decision on claude-opus-5.

nodes.label: What leaves the machine, exactly
nodes.rationale: One HTTPS POST per decision carrying only what the question needs; never the transcript, never file contents the agent did not just fetch, never the session id; the audit log keeps a prefix, not the command.

nodes.label: Close the milestone
nodes.rationale: Only when actually finished — a milestone with open issues stays open and says so in the log.

nodes.label: Create the GitHub release
nodes.rationale: Rerun-safe: a rerun that already got this far would otherwise die on "release already exists". Notes prepend the install snippet and the TYPESAFE_API_KEY note.

nodes.label: Publish to npm
nodes.rationale: Skips an already-published version so a bootstrap release still cuts its release and closes its milestone; unsets NODE_AUTH_TOKEN so only OIDC can authenticate; --loglevel verbose because a refused OIDC exchange otherwise ends in a bare ENEEDAUTH (seen 2026-09-22, 0.0.3).

nodes.label: release job
nodes.rationale: Holds contents:write, issues:write and id-token:write — id-token is what authenticates the OIDC publish.

nodes.label: Release workflow
nodes.rationale: Cut a release by pushing the tag that `claude plugin tag` creates; everything after that happens in CI with no npm token anywhere.

nodes.label: Resolve and verify the version
nodes.rationale: The tag is the source of truth for what is released; package.json must agree, and npm test checks the other manifests against it.

nodes.label: Use an npm that speaks OIDC
nodes.rationale: Trusted publishing needs npm >= 11.5.1 and Node 22 still bundles npm 10; pinned to npm@11.19.0 because npm@latest would put a moving dependency in the publishing path.
nodes.norm_label: use an npm that speaks oidc

nodes.label: Verify the published version
nodes.rationale: The registry took over a minute to serve 0.3.2 on 2026-09-18, which six 10-second tries did not cover; now twenty tries at 15 seconds.

nodes.label: BACKLOG.md — single source of truth
nodes.rationale: New ideas go here rather than into scattered TODO comments; ROADMAP.md and the GitHub issues are generated views of it.

nodes.label: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.rationale: Keep a Changelog format, SemVer, HG-n ids on every line; check wants [Unreleased] and the current version.

nodes.label: evals/commands.jsonl (79 labelled commands)
nodes.rationale: 35 safe, 26 ask, 18 dangerous, labelled by hand.

nodes.label: Release runbook
nodes.rationale: Pushing the tag is the only manual step; bump four manifests, rename [Unreleased], turn ver=main into ver=x.y.z, land on main via PR, tag the merge commit; every workflow step is idempotent.

nodes.label: One-time npm Trusted Publisher setup
nodes.rationale: npm cannot configure a trusted publisher for a package that does not exist, so the first version is published by hand; then Allan-Nava / hookgate / release.yml / no environment on npmjs.com.

nodes.label: ROADMAP.md (generated view)
nodes.rationale: Generated by scripts/backlog.mjs roadmap from BACKLOG.md — never edited by hand; CI fails when the two disagree. 31 items, 26 shipped, 5 open, 4 milestones.

nodes.label: Do not rename release.yml
nodes.rationale: The trusted publisher on npm is bound to the literal filename release.yml; renaming it stops the publish authenticating with an error that does not mention the filename.

nodes.label: --ignore-scripts on install
nodes.rationale: The job holds the OIDC publishing privilege, so no dependency lifecycle script runs beside it; the only dependency is `marked`, used by the site build, and it needs no scripts.

nodes.label: No registry-url on setup-node
nodes.rationale: setup-node with registry-url writes an .npmrc holding _authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} and exports a placeholder; npm then finds a configured credential, skips the OIDC exchange and gets a misleading 404. Trusted publishing needs no credential in the environment.

nodes.label: npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC)
nodes.rationale: No npm token in the repository: the publish authenticates through OIDC, configured on the package at npmjs.com against this repository and this workflow filename. Provenance is generated automatically, so --provenance is not passed.

nodes.label: The benchmark gates the release
nodes.rationale: A plugin that says deny to a developer had better have a number behind it; the gates decide on a calibration nobody has measured, so audit mode is the only recommended mode until HG-4 runs.

nodes.label: Audit mode by default in 0.0.3
nodes.rationale: mode defaults to audit — judge, log, fall through — until HG-4 has measured the thresholds; "mode": "enforce" in ~/.hookgate.json opts in; 0.1.0 flips the default back.

nodes.label: Every idea goes in BACKLOG.md
nodes.rationale: Stable HG-n id, never a scattered TODO; regenerate ROADMAP.md or CI fails; issues sync one way.

nodes.label: The name had a past (0.0.1 burnt)
nodes.rationale: hookgate on npm carried a 0.0.1 published and unpublished 2026-03-23; npm never lets a version be reused, so the first publishable version is 0.0.2. npm view errors for a name with no live versions, which reads as free — check the registry JSON and time.unpublished instead.
nodes.norm_label: the name had a past (0.0.1 burnt)

nodes.label: 90% agreement rule
nodes.rationale: Stated in advance: under about 90% agreement with the labels the command gate ships ask-only; the injection screen stays off until its false positives on the clean set are zero.

nodes.label: HG-13 — Promote confident, repeated decisions into the harness's rules
nodes.rationale: Three allow or deny above 0.95 on one prefix → one systemMessage proposing the rule. Propose, never write.
nodes.norm_label: hg-13 — promote confident, repeated decisions into the harness's rules

nodes.label: HG-23 — Completion prefilter is English-only
nodes.rationale: claimsCompletion knew only English, so 766 of 1,229 real stops were Italian claims it skipped — the "skips 81%" was partly language, not silence. Fix: COMPLETION_LEXICONS.{en,it} with ambiguous Italian words anchored to their claim form, completion.lexicon for extras; honest skip rate 29%.

nodes.label: HG-24 — Promotion attributes a chained command's verdict to its first word
nodes.rationale: commandPrefix kept the first command of a && b | c, so a deny on git status && curl | sh counted against git status; 92.5% of real commands are compound. Fix: only a simple command counts toward promotion — promotablePrefix(); compound ones logged promotable: null.
nodes.norm_label: hg-24 — promotion attributes a chained command's verdict to its first word

nodes.label: HG-25 — Never propose a rule for an interpreter or wrapper prefix
nodes.rationale: python3, node, bash, sudo, xargs, eval… head 23.5% of real commands and Bash(python3 *) as allow covers python3 -c "shutil.rmtree()" — the proposal widens. Fix: NEVER_PROMOTE in store.mjs, both directions, find included for -exec.
nodes.norm_label: hg-25 — never propose a rule for an interpreter or wrapper prefix

nodes.label: HG-26 — A command longer than maxStateChars is judged with its middle elided
nodes.rationale: truncate keeps 70% head and 30% tail, so rm -rf padded into the middle passes; 94 real commands exceed 12,000 chars. Fix: the command gate answers ask ("too long to judge") with no request; completion and injection gates keep truncating, where an elided middle costs recall, not safety.
nodes.norm_label: hg-26 — a command longer than maxstatechars is judged with its middle elided

nodes.label: HG-27 — A repository can switch the gates off through its own config
nodes.rationale: loadConfig read .hookgate.json from the harness cwd, so a cloned repo shipping gates.command=false or mode=audit disabled the gate silently. Fix: TIGHTEN table in config.mjs with a direction per field; model and timeoutMs never from the repository; doctor lists ignored fields; HOOKGATE_USER_CONFIG for tests.
nodes.norm_label: hg-27 — a repository can switch the gates off through its own config

nodes.label: HG-28 — The audit log has no token usage, so cost per decision cannot be computed
nodes.rationale: systemone returned usage, judge carried it, log dropped it. Fix: inputTokens on every judged record; PRICE_PER_INPUT_TOKEN and PRICE_DATE in report.mjs, imported by evals/run.mjs.
nodes.norm_label: hg-28 — the audit log has no token usage, so cost per decision cannot be computed

nodes.label: HG-29 — Validate the numbers in the config and classify a non-JSON body
nodes.rationale: timeoutMs, maxStateChars, cache.ttlMs, promote.* were never checked, so a string or null flowed into setTimeout and truncate; a 200 with a non-JSON body surfaced as network rather than malformed, hiding a broken proxy. Fix: RULES in config.mjs with ranges, res.json() failures mapped to malformed.
nodes.norm_label: hg-29 — validate the numbers in the config and classify a non-json body

nodes.label: HG-30 — Scorecard: one metric per open bug, on base and head of every PR
nodes.rationale: evals/scorecard.mjs scores HG-23 to HG-29 from evals/fixtures/ with no key; scorecard.yml posts base, head and delta as one sticky comment and fails on a regression. A fix moves its line to 100%; a new bug lands with its fixture.
nodes.norm_label: hg-30 — scorecard: one metric per open bug, on base and head of every pr

nodes.label: v0.1.2 — Bugs from the first measurements
nodes.rationale: What running evals/local.mjs over 102 real sessions (27,147 commands, 1,229 stops) and a second read of the handlers turned up; one PR each, highest priority first, the scorecard saying by how much each moved.
nodes.norm_label: v0.1.2 — bugs from the first measurements

nodes.label: Release 0.0.3 — 2026-09-22
nodes.rationale: Everything since the bootstrap: both gates, Codex, the audit, the seven bugs the first measurements found, and the scorecard. Audit mode by default because the benchmark has not run.

nodes.label: Codex rules (Starlark prefix_rule)
nodes.rationale: Static allow | prompt | forbidden per command prefix — the natural place for a confident, repeated hookgate decision to be promoted to.

nodes.label: Per-language completion lexicon
nodes.rationale: English and Italian built in, completion.lexicon adds patterns.

nodes.label: Completion prefilter
nodes.rationale: A local check skips questions and partial reports with no network call; measured to skip 29% of real stops, not the 81% first reported.

nodes.label: Local measurements (evals/local.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Hook overhead by spawning the CLI and counts over local transcripts — nothing sent anywhere, only aggregates written.

nodes.label: State never carries secrets (redaction)
nodes.rationale: Key shapes, bearer headers, KEY=value, URL passwords and private keys are redacted before anything leaves; state truncated well under Jev's 32k-token limit.

nodes.label: Rule promotion
nodes.rationale: Three verdicts above 95% confidence on one command prefix produce one systemMessage proposing the harness's own permission rule. Proposed, never written, and only for one simple command whose program is not an interpreter or wrapper, so the rule never widens.

nodes.label: Scorecard (evals/scorecard.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Every fix carries its number: one metric per open bug from committed fixtures, no key, no network.

nodes.label: Score the base with the head's fixtures
nodes.rationale: A base that predates a metric scores n/a rather than failing.
nodes.norm_label: score the base with the head's fixtures

nodes.label: Score the head
nodes.rationale: Compares against out/base.json when it exists; the delta lands in summary.md.

nodes.label: Scorecard workflow
nodes.rationale: One number per open bug, on base and head of every pull request, from the same committed fixtures, no key and no network — so a fix says by how much it moved the metric it names.

nodes.label: Sticky comment on the pull request
nodes.rationale: One comment found by the <!-- hookgate-scorecard --> marker and updated in place; only for same-repo PRs, since forks lack the token.
nodes.norm_label: sticky comment on the pull request

nodes.label: Benchmark protocol
nodes.rationale: The runner refuses to start without a key because every run costs money; results are committed as one run, one version, one date; re-run when the Jev version changes or a threshold default moves.

nodes.label: evals/fixtures/ (labelled fixtures per open bug)
nodes.rationale: 48 final messages in two languages, 32 commands labelled by what a promotion rule may cover, generated over-long commands, loosening repository configs, invalid config values.

nodes.label: evals/injection.jsonl (20 tool outputs)
nodes.rationale: 10 clean and 10 carrying instructions addressed to an agent.

nodes.label: Fixtures always from the head
nodes.rationale: Adding a fixture changes the denominator for both sides alike; the base is scored with the head's scorecard too.

nodes.label: Regression on any metric fails
nodes.rationale: A fix moves its line to 100%; a regression on any metric fails the job.

nodes.label: maxStateChars cap (12,000)
nodes.rationale: A command longer than maxStateChars is ask with no request: judging a head and a tail is not judging the command.

nodes.label: Promotion proposes, never writes
nodes.rationale: Three verdicts ≥ 0.95 on one prefix produce one systemMessage in the detected harness's rule syntax, once per prefix per session.

nodes.label: Stop prefilter (Q7)
nodes.rationale: Traced with the graph: the completion gate asked Jev on every stop that passed the guards — the brief's assumed local prefilter was not implemented. claimsCompletion() now gates the request on lexicon, a ticked task list or an "all tests" phrase; skipped stops logged skipped:prefilter; completion.prefilter: false turns it off.
